items.title: The Old Game Is Over: Shift to GEO and Search Everywhere Optimization
items.summary: Traditional SEO focused on keywords and backlinks is ending as AI like Google’s AI Overviews and ChatGPT answer queries directly without clicks. Impressions increase but clicks drop significantly, with data showing 357% YoY growth in AI referrals yet 4x CTR drops. The future lies in Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), proprietary data, and optimizing across platforms like TikTok and Reddit.

items.title: SEO Evolving into Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)
items.summary: SEO is no longer about ranking in blue links but being included in AI-generated answers from ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI. GEO requires structuring content for AI to understand, trust, extract, and cite it effectively. Success demands topical authority, machine-readable formats, and real expertise.

items.title: Try This Underused Tactic To Get Your Content Cited in AI Search
items.summary: Marketers aim to have their content cited by AI search engines like ChatGPT and Perplexity. The article shares an underused tactic along with expert insights to boost citation chances through generative engine optimization. Optimizing for AI visibility is key in the evolving search landscape.

items.title: Why ‘search everywhere’ is the new reality for SEO
items.summary: Traditional SEO is insufficient as users search across Google, social media, TikTok, Reddit, and AI tools. Strategies must optimize content for discovery on all platforms where audiences query. This 'search everywhere' approach defines modern SEO success.

items.title: Hachette Book Group pulls horror novel 'Shy Girl' after AI writing allegations
items.summary: Hachette Book Group canceled the US release of Mia Ballard's horror novel 'Shy Girl' following widespread online allegations and evidence that AI was used in its writing. The book, originally self-published and buzzy on BookTok, was acquired by a major publisher but pulled after AI detection tools flagged 78% of the content. This marks the first major traditional publishing cancellation over AI use, sparking debates on detection and ethics.

items.title: Lake Union Publishing acquires 'After the Storm' by Lorna Lewis
items.summary: Lake Union Publishing announced a major deal for 'After the Storm' by Lorna Lewis, a gripping contemporary fiction novel about a woman rescued as a child and raised by strangers. Acquired by agent Michelle Jackson, the book is set for fall 2027 publication. The acquisition highlights ongoing interest in emotional family dramas.

items.title: Book review: 'Arctic Dreams and Nightmares' blends traditional Inuit storytelling with modern references
items.summary: The reissued book 'Arctic Dreams and Nightmares' by Alootook Ipellie combines traditional Inuit storytelling with contemporary cultural clashes. Reviewer praises its exploration of character dynamics amid rapid changes in Arctic communities. This release revives important Indigenous voices in literature.

items.title: PopCrave reports Hachette pulls 'Shy Girl' horror novel over AI claims
items.summary: PopCrave shared news that Hachette Book Group pulled the upcoming 'Shy Girl' after reader allegations of AI-generated content. The post garnered massive engagement, highlighting the viral nature of the scandal. Includes promotional images of the book.

items.title: 'Shy Girl' author Mia Ballard releases statement denying AI use
items.summary: Author Mia Ballard responded to the cancellation of her novel 'Shy Girl', claiming she did not use AI and that the controversy has ruined her name and mental health. She mentioned pursuing legal action but provided no further details on editing process. Posted by PopCrave with images.

items.title: K.T. Carlisle questions how 'Shy Girl' AI scandal evaded traditional publishing gatekeepers
items.summary: Author K.T. Carlisle lists key unanswered questions about the 'Shy Girl' scandal, including how an AI-written manuscript passed agent, editor, and Big 5 scrutiny. Demands details on definitive AI detection methods beyond public outcry. Quotes NYT article on the pull.

items.title: ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ Makes Oscars History With Original Song Win for “Golden”
items.summary: The Netflix animated feature KPop Demon Hunters, which follows a K-pop girl group fighting demons, won Best Animated Feature and Best Original Song for “Golden” at the 2026 Oscars, marking a historic achievement as Netflix's most popular title with its soundtrack topping charts. Directors Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans accepted the award, emphasizing representation for Koreans, while performers highlighted resilience. The film's success underscores K-pop's breakthrough in mainstream entertainment.

items.title: Oscars was so keen to not be woke, it ended up being woker than ever
items.summary: The 2026 Oscars aimed to sidestep wokeness with neutral hosting by Conan O'Brien but amplified off-script political remarks from winners and presenters on Palestine, wars, and free speech. Balanced diversity and apologies for past underrepresentation made the event feel even more woke despite efforts to tone it down. The approach backfired, spotlighting progressive elements.

items.title: Hollywood went broke ramming woke propaganda down non-woke Americans' throats
items.summary: Hollywood has bankrupted itself by forcing propaganda on 90% of Americans who aren't woke, leading to industry declines. Trump allies gaining control of CNN and major studios signal turning tides. Links to an article on corporate America's repeated hard lessons.

items.title: Woke hype for pandering films fails to deliver box office support
items.summary: Woke individuals hype virtue-signaling films like The Marvels, 2016 Ghostbusters, and Birds of Prey but refuse to buy tickets or support them financially, causing flops. This pattern continues with The Bride and 1348 Ex Voto. Pandering to this group is the worst long-term strategy for brands.

items.title: Out Of Touch Hollywood Throws Woke Oscars Amid Box Office Crashes
items.summary: Despite 50% production drops, 40% box office crashes, and tanking ratings, the Oscars featured a woke celebration including a flop Antifa-themed Best Picture. Disney's Snow White bombed $170M due to princess-hating and CGI fails. Get woke, go broke.

items.title: NeuralFlow AI: Bootstrapped AI Automation Empowering Small Businesses
items.summary: NeuralFlow AI is being developed from Bayonne, NJ, without VC funding, big teams, or external support. It focuses on delivering AI solutions that help small businesses generate more revenue, challenging the notion that advanced technology is reserved for enterprises only. The tool is available at neuralflowai.io for small businesses seeking accessible AI.

items.title: Codie Sanchez Predicts AI-Powered Small Business Boom
items.summary: Codie Sanchez highlights the impending largest small business boom ever, enabled by AI tools allowing a single person with a laptop and niche audience to replicate the output of a 15-person team costing $200K. She urges locking in efforts over the next two years to build generational wealth despite AI skepticism. This shift democratizes business scaling for individuals.

items.title: Durable Launches End-to-End AI Platform for Small Businesses
items.summary: Durable has unveiled an enhanced AI platform that supports entrepreneurs in running entire businesses, extending far beyond simple website creation. The tool aims to normalize small business ownership by providing comprehensive AI-driven operations. It's positioned to lower barriers for new and existing small business owners.

items.title: Promptory Debuts Curated AI Marketplace with Strategy Director for SMBs
items.summary: The Promptory has launched the first curated marketplace of over 100 vetted AI tools tailored for small businesses and enterprises. It features a built-in AI Strategy Director to assist with adoption and implementation. The release aligns with surging interest in AI among small business owners seeking practical solutions.
